messages.author: 14f33f5ab5b4a1db
messages.subject: inla.dmarginal returning sparse densities
parts:
Hello,

I am encountering a problem where the likelihoods returned from inla.dmarginal are frequently all 0 or nearly all 0. This seems to occur when most of my observations have similar inputs.

For example, my data set is ~290,000 observations. If I use run a model with 2 fixed effects and 2 random effects, where the number of unique values for each feature is 17, 104, 14, and 5, inla.dmarginal returns all 0s.

If I add in a factor the value of which is 1:n for my n observations, I get non-zero densities everywhere.

If many observations have the same input values is dmarginal unreliable?

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.dmarginal returning sparse densities
parts:

try to ask for the log-density value, which is the only one that is
reliable (in general with densitites),

inla.dmarginal(...., log=TRUE)


if this does not help, I need to rerun it here, then please send R-code
and data (or some similar data)

messages.author: 14f33f5ab5b4a1db
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.dmarginal returning sparse densities
parts:
Unfortunately all the densities are exactly 0 so log=TRUE returns -Inf everywhere.

Attached is some data. Features FE1 and FE2 are continuous fixed effects, RE1, RE2, and RE3 are string values converted to factors. Using any combination of these features I have tried results in dmarginal of 0 for all observations, or nearly all of them. Adding in participant_id starts to make sense. target is the response variable and has NA values for the last 25% of the data to function as a test set for cross validation.

Here is what my model call looks like:

m1 <- inla(target ~ 1

    # Fixed Effects
    + FE1
    + FE2

    # Random Effects
    + f(RE1,                     model='iid', hyper=hyper_RE1)
    + f(RE2,                     model='iid', hyper=hyper_RE2)
    + f(RE3,                     model='iid', hyper=hyper_RE3)
    + f(participant_id,    model='ii'd, hyper=hyper_participant_id)

    , data=df, family="gaussian"
    , control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, config=TRUE)
    , control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive",  int.strategy="auto", cmin=0)
    , verbose=T
    )

The value of the hyper used for each random effect is list(theta = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(5.4087488057048, 0.05)))

seconds.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.dmarginal returning sparse densities
parts: mapply(inla.dmarginal, rdata[1:100,]$target, m1$marginals.fitted.values[1:100]) this should be fairly fast.
